what_is_quest.title: What Quest is
what_is_quest.text:
Quest helps you set a transformative goal and reach it. You describe what you want, Quest turns it into an evidence-backed plan, and then you track it, reflect on it, and adjust it over time. You can do all of this alone, or bring in an AI assistant, a mentor, a team, or a community.

## What you can do with it

You do not have to use all of this. Pick what helps.

- **Plan from evidence.** Run a [Deep Inquiry](/guide/deep-inquiries) to research your goal across the [perspectives](/guide/perspectives) you choose, then accept the strategies you want.
- **Run a plan day to day.** Your [plan](/guide/quests-and-plans) becomes milestones, dated goals, and recurring habits on a Today view and a Schedule.
- **Talk to [Quest AI](/guide/quest-ai).** Ask it to adjust a plan, add a goal, or do work for you.
- **Reflect.** A short [daily reflection and period reviews](/guide/productivity) keep you on pace.
- **Track anything** with free [Data Collections](/data-collections/).
- **Bring people in.** Get a [mentor](/guide/mentors), share quests with a [team](/guide/teams), or join [communities](/guide/communities).

plans_table.title: Plans and pricing: at a glance
plans_table.text:
Quest has a useful free plan, a full trial, and two paid subscriptions. This page is the reference for what each one includes. Prices are in US dollars.

## At a glance

| | Free | 31 day trial | Quest AI | Quest Guided |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Price | $0 | $0 | $10/mo or $100/yr | $50/mo or $500/yr |
| Quick quests | Up to 1,000 | Up to 1,000 | Up to 1,000 | Up to 1,000 |
| AI-assisted quest creation | No | Up to 1,000 | Up to 1,000 | Up to 1,000 |
| Deep Inquiries and scientific analysis of your goals | No | Up to 50/day | Up to 50/day | Up to 50/day |
| [Science](/guide/science) Direct searches | 10/day | 20/day | Up to 1,000/day | Up to 1,000/day |
| Quest AI chat | Answers questions about how Quest works only | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| AI tasks (delegated work) | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| AI plan generation | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Daily reflection and period reviews | Yes | Yes (with AI insights) | Yes (with AI insights) | Yes (with AI insights) |
| Data Collections | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Community chat | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Human coaching | No | No | No | Yes |

plans_free.title: Plans and pricing: the Free plan
plans_free.text:
## Free

The Free plan is genuinely useful on its own. This is the written record of what free users get, and the same list appears on the billing screen and the public pricing page. Check each line against the product before you change it.

- **Up to 1,000 quests that you plan yourself.** These are quick quests: you build the goals and habits.
- **Daily reflection and period reviews** for week, month, quarter, and year.
- **Data Collections and notes** for your own data, with full export.
- **Quest's communities.** Join planets and towns and invite anyone.
- **Quest AI chat for how Quest works.** It answers questions about the app. On Free it cannot read or change your quests.
- **Web and mobile apps.**
- **A free 31 day trial of Quest AI.**

The Free plan does not include AI-assisted quest creation, Quest AI chat that works on your quests, AI tasks, AI plan generation, Deep Inquiries and scientific analysis of your goals, or AI insights in your reflections and reviews (the daily reflection and period reviews themselves stay free, and so does what you already saved). When you reach for one of those, Quest invites you to start the trial or subscribe.

plans_trial.title: Plans and pricing: the 31 day trial
plans_trial.text:
## The 31 day trial

When you create your account, a **31 day free trial of Quest AI** begins. During the trial you get the full Quest AI experience: AI-assisted quest creation up to 1,000 quests, AI plan generation, up to 50 Deep Inquiries a day, Quest AI chat, AI tasks, and AI insights in your reflections and reviews.

When the trial ends, you keep everything you made. You move to the Free plan unless you subscribe.

plans_quest_ai.title: Plans and pricing: Quest AI
plans_quest_ai.text:
## Quest AI

**$10 per month, or $100 per year.** Everything in the trial, ongoing:

- AI-assisted quest creation, up to 1,000 quests.
- Up to 50 Deep Inquiries per day. A Deep Inquiry looks at your goal from several expert perspectives and draws on research and people's real experiences, then uses what it finds to suggest strategies that fit you. It takes a few minutes.
- Quest AI chat with the ability to act on your quests, and AI tasks that run delegated work.
- AI plan generation: strategies and goals written for a quest.
- AI insights in daily reflections and period reviews, including the written proposals for suggested changes to your plan. See [Insights](/guide/insights#plans).

share_howto.title: How-to: share one goal
share_howto.text:
## I want to share one goal with my partner or coach, but keep the rest private

Invite them to **that single quest** by email. Your other quests stay private. For a group that owns goals together, use a [team](/guide/teams) instead. See [Sharing a quest](/guide/quests-and-plans#sharing-a-quest).

share_guide.title: Quests and plans: sharing a quest
share_guide.text:
## Sharing a quest

Quests are private to you by default. When you want help on one, you have two options.

- **Share with a person.** Invite someone by email to a single quest. Your other quests stay private. This is good for a friend, partner, or accountability buddy. If they already have a Quest account, they also get a notification (push and in-app) about the invitation, in addition to the email, so they do not have to be watching their inbox to notice it.
- **Share with a team.** Put a quest on a team's shelf so a whole group owns and moves it together, with roles and assignments. On the quest's dashboard, tap **More**, then **Share with a team** (shown when you are on at least one team), or add it from the team page. See [Teams](/guide/teams).

habit_howto.title: How-to: add a recurring action
habit_howto.text:
## I want to add a recurring action, like meditate every morning

Add a **habit**. Give it a schedule (for example, every weekday morning) and it will appear on **Today** and **Schedule**. Log it each time as done, partial, or not. See [Habits](/guide/quests-and-plans#habits).

calendar_howto.title: How-to: Quest and your calendar
calendar_howto.text:
## I want Quest to know about my real calendar

Go to **Settings > Calendar Sync** and connect Google Calendar or a calendar from your phone. Under **Calendar to Quest**, turn on "Show events on Quest and use for AI scheduling" so your events appear in Quest as goals and inform your Schedule and the AI's scheduling suggestions, and under **Quest to Calendar** turn on "Add Quest schedule to this calendar" if you also want your goals and habits written out to it. See [Calendar Sync](/guide/calendar-sync).

quest_ai_recording.title: Quest AI: recording things as you go
quest_ai_recording.text:
### Recording things as you go

You can record your day straight into a quest from chat, in a sentence:

- "Mark my morning run habit done for today." It shows as done on Today's Actions, the same as tapping Done.
- "I stretched for 15 minutes, log that against my stretching habit." The minutes count toward the habit's daily target. Under the target it shows as started, at or over it as done.

first_quest_intro.title: Create your first quest: before you start
first_quest_intro.text:
# Create your first quest

This walkthrough takes you through creating an AI-assisted quest from start to finish. Plan about 15 to 20 minutes for the first one. You can leave and come back; your progress is saved as you go.

If you want a lightweight quest with no AI, make a **quick quest** instead. It uses the same plan structure but skips the research steps and the full specification, and it is always free. A quest is the specification of one intention plus its plan, not a checklist, so tasks with no outcome behind them belong in your goals and habits.

## Before you start

A quest works best when the goal is real and a little ambitious. Compare:

- Vague: "be healthier", "be happier", "learn Spanish".
- Strong: "reduce my anxiety by half and meditate daily within 6 months", "move from a corporate job to freelance coaching within a year", "develop measurable remote-viewing accuracy over 100 logged sessions".

A strong goal names an end state you will reach, a way to tell you reached it, and a rough timeframe. You can refine all of this with the AI, so a rough version is fine to start.

first_quest_context.title: Create your first quest: step 2, context
first_quest_context.text:
### Measurable outcomes (Metrics)

*How will you know it is real?* These become the Metrics that show your vision is real. Check your vision, write why it matters, then list your measurable outcomes: one per line, each with its number or threshold, such as "I run 60 km a week". Tap **Get AI suggestions** to have Quest score your vision and outcomes and propose better ones, then **Use these outcomes** to take them. When you started from a spec and have no outcomes yet, the lines start from the spec's most common metrics, adapted to you.

On **Continue**, each line is saved as a measurable outcome. Quest reads the target number and unit from your wording (60 and km in the example) and never adds one you did not write. A line that matches an outcome you already have keeps its progress. If the targets cannot be read, your outcomes are still saved, without numbers.

### Current state (Problems)

*Where are you now, and what have you tried?* Next, the AI turns this into the Problems your strategies address. Tell Quest where you are starting from: what is in the way, what you have already tried and how it went, and facts with numbers and dates where you have them. As you write, Quest may ask follow-up questions; tap **Ask more questions** for another round.

### Preferences (Ideals)

*What principles must your strategies honor, and what will you not do?* These become the Ideals every strategy must honor: the values, tradition, limits and qualities every strategy has to respect, plus the approaches and tools you favor or refuse, such as "no medication" or "30 minutes each morning".

core_quest.title: Core concepts: quest and its specification
core_quest.text:
## Quest

A **quest** is the specification of one intention of yours, plus the plan that carries it out. The specification says where you want to end up (the outcome), why it matters (the purpose), where you stand now and what you have tried (the current state), how you will know you arrived (the acceptance criteria), and what you prefer. Around it sit your plan, progress, reflections, and any people or AI helping you. A quest is not a checklist, and most things in the app hang off a quest.

You can have many quests at once. Each quest lives in a life category (a [planet](#planets-towns-and-the-galaxy)) such as Health, Relationships, or Spirituality.

There are two ways to make one:

- **Quick quest:** a lightweight quest: you write the outcome and plan yourself, without the full specification. Always free, no AI required.
- **AI-assisted quest:** Quest interviews you, can run a Deep Inquiry, and builds the plan with you. Included in the trial and paid plans.

## Outcome, purpose, current state and the rest of the specification

When you create a quest you describe the intention behind it:

- **Vision statement**: one short sentence naming an end state you will reach at some point, such as "I have finished a marathon". It is not a permanent quality ("I am always calm") and not a task.
- **Name**: a short label for the quest, shown in lists, drop-downs, Today and the plan. Quest writes one from your vision statement; you can change it any time. A quest with no name yet shows its vision statement where a label is needed, and its Name field says so instead of repeating the vision statement. The name and vision statement of a quest are those of the intent it sits alone under, so editing either one updates the other.
- **Acceptance criteria** (the Measurable Outcomes card): three to six high level signs that the outcome is real, each with a number, threshold or named measurement, such as "finish a full marathon in under 5 hours". They are never tasks.
- **Measurable outcomes** (the checklist under that card): the numbers you track, each with a target and a unit, derived from the acceptance criteria.
- **Purpose:** why it matters to you, in your own reasons.
- **Current state:** the problems in your way and the solutions you have already tried, with how they went.
- **Preferences:** the approaches and tools you prefer or refuse, the principles a plan should respect, and what you would like measured.

Quest uses these to keep plans realistic and personal. Good plans depend on an honest current state. The exact definitions of each field are kept in one place, the field guidance Quest AI follows, and these pages summarize them.

reflection.title: Productivity workflow: daily reflection
reflection.text:
## Daily reflection

The daily reflection is a short check-in that bookends your day. It reads top to bottom as one train of thought in two parts: **what happened**, then **what's next**. Each part sits in its own colored box, and tapping a part's heading folds it away so you can focus on the other. Under the title, a **Today / Tomorrow** switch sets which day you are reviewing and planning for.

- **How did yesterday go?** Write or speak (tap the mic) what went well, what was hard, and what you learned. When you click out of the box, your AI can split what you wrote into short notes under the quests they concern. Each note shows its quest underneath (for example "Quest: Career"); tap it to pick a different quest. You can edit, move, or delete any note before you continue, and nothing is saved to a quest until you do.

- **What's your plan?** Describe the day in plain words, with times if you have them ("Meditate at 7am, work on the proposal 9 to 12, call Mom at 2pm"). On the next screen Quest turns it into individual goals for you to check.

period_reviews.title: Productivity workflow: period reviews
period_reviews.text:
A period review is a longer reflection for a **week, month, quarter, or year**. Each one helps you look back and plan forward:

- See your stats and what you completed in the period.

- Reflect on how it went.

- Go through what you did not finish and choose, per goal, whether to move it forward, keep it, or abandon it.

- Get suggested goals for the next period, and accept the ones you want straight into your plan.

### Trajectory

For **measurable goals**, a period review shows a trajectory: it compares your logged data against each goal's target and tells you whether you are **ahead, on track, at risk, or already achieved**. This turns a vague "am I doing okay?" into a clear read on pace, early enough to adjust. Set a target number on a goal to get this (see [Goals](/guide/quests-and-plans#goals)).

collections.title: Data Collections: what they are
collections.text:
# Data Collections

Data Collections are Quest's flexible logs for any recurring data: dreams, journals, workouts, moods, practice sessions, symptoms, anything you want to track over time. You define the fields, add entries, and export everything whenever you like.

Collections are **free for everyone**, on every plan, with or without an active quest. If all you want is a good dream journal, Quest is as simple as a dedicated app. When you need more, the same tool scales to detailed, structured tracking.

## What a collection is

A collection has a name, an icon and color, and a set of **fields** that define what each entry records. Add entries over time, and each one captures the fields you defined plus the date. You can tag entries, search them, and filter them.

## Creating a collection

Create a collection from scratch, or start from a template and adjust it. Common starting points:

- **Dream journal:** date, mood on waking, lucidity rating, the dream itself, symbols, tags.
- **Daily journal:** date, mood, gratitude, challenges, insights, energy level.
- **Practice or session log:** date, technique, duration, outcome, notes.

You can also browse collections that others have made public and use one as your starting point, then customize it.

## Collections and quests

Collections can stand alone, or feed your quests:

- **Link a collection to a quest** so the data you log there is part of that quest's context. Open the collection's settings, find **Linked Quests**, and search your quests by name to link one. You never need a quest id.
- A habit you track is itself a small collection under the hood, which is why habit entries can carry rich custom fields.

Linking is optional. Many people keep a journal or dream log with no quest attached at all. When you do link one, the patterns in your data give Quest and your [Deep Inquiries](/guide/deep-inquiries) real material to personalize your plan.

habit_tracking_types.title: Quests and plans: habits and tracking types
habit_tracking_types.text:
### Habits

Habits are actions you repeat on a schedule: "meditate 10 minutes each morning", "log one practice session three times a week". When you log a habit you record whether you did it fully, partly, or not, and you can attach custom fields so the entry captures real detail (see [Data Collections](/data-collections/)). Habits are where most day-to-day progress comes from.

### Tracking types

When you create a habit, you choose what to track:

- **Simple check-in.** Mark yes, partial, or no each time. For example, morning meditation.
- **Frequency-based.** Complete a target number of times per period (day, week, or month, taken from the habit's frequency). For example, exercise three times a week.
- **Quantity.** Track a measurable amount against a target. For example, read 30 pages.
- **Timer.** Track time spent with a countdown or a stopwatch, with a session length and an optional period goal. For example, practice piano 45 minutes.

life_design.title: Life design
life_design.text:
# Life design

Life design is a short set of questions that helps you name what you are living for, then gives your quests somewhere to sit. You answer once, in about five minutes, and you can come back to your answers whenever you like.

It is optional. If you never start it, your quest list works exactly as it always has.

## Why it exists

A long list of quests tells you what you are doing, not why. Life design adds one level above your quests: a few **top intents**, short statements of what you want your life to be about, such as "A body that carries me" or "Work that matters". Each quest then belongs to one intent, and your quest list groups them that way.

esoi_brief.title: Quest and ESOI: in brief
esoi_brief.text:
Quest is designed with a framework called **Evolvable Structure that Optimizes Intent** (ESOI). This section describes the Quest product in ESOI's terms: what Quest is for, what it is defined to do, and where each part of a quest fits. It describes the product as people use it, not how it is built.

## ESOI in brief

ESOI turns an intention into a structure that gets better at fulfilling it over time, and that can change when the intention changes. Every intent is written as five kinds of record, linked to each other:

experiments_intro.title: Experiments
experiments_intro.text:
# Experiments

Quest stands for **Qualitative Understanding Enables Self-Transformation**. The Experiments section on a quest's dashboard is where that becomes literal. You ask a research question about your quest, see what existing evidence says about it, then test the answer in your own life and let the AI read what your data shows.

There are two ways to answer a question, and the best experiments use both:

- **Existing evidence.** Tap **Run deep inquiry** to research the question across research papers and real lived experiences, the same way quest creation does.
- **Your own life.** Link the habits, collections and goals that gather data for the question, then tap **Analyze my data**.

mentee_find.title: Mentors: finding a mentor
mentee_find.text:
# Mentors

A mentor is a real person who guides you through your quest with paid check-ins. Quest connects people who want guidance with people qualified to give it, and handles the scheduling and payment around it.

Mentors are optional. Many people run quests with only the AI and the community. A mentor adds human accountability and judgment when you want it.

## Finding a mentor

Open **Mentorship** in the Community section. It is the home for everything mentoring: your conversations with the people mentoring you and the people you mentor, plus **Find a mentor** and **Become a mentor**. Find a mentor opens a guided search where you describe what you want help with in your own words, or start from a topic, and see mentors whose experience fits. If you want to know how it works first, **How being a mentee works** explains what a mentee is, what it costs, and how matching and check-ins work.

Search mentors and look at their background, credentials, and focus areas. When you find a good fit, you connect with them and can link the mentor to the quest they are helping you with, so they see the context that matters.

mentee_pay.title: Mentors: paying a mentor
mentee_pay.text:
### Paying a mentor

There is no subscription to a mentor and you never type in an amount. You add dollar credit to your own balance by card, and credit is spent on a mentor only when a check-in takes place.

- **Add credit.** Add credit to your balance by card from your balance screen. This is a one-time payment, not a recurring charge. Money you added by card is used first, then any credit you have earned. Card money cannot be withdrawn as cash. On a phone, the card page opens inside the app and closes by itself when you finish or cancel; Quest then waits for your payment to arrive and tells you when the credit has been added, which can take a few seconds. If you close the page yourself, nothing is wrong: if you did pay, the credit appears shortly.
- **Choose a tier.** A mentor offers one or more check-in tiers. A tier is a named package with one fixed price per check-in, and you pick the one you want when you request the mentor. You need at least that tier's total in your balance to request the mentor. If you do not have enough, the app asks you to add credit. Requesting a mentor does not charge you.
- **Service fee.** On the Free and Quest AI plans, each check-in carries a 5% service fee on top of the mentor's price, so your mentor always receives their full price. On Quest Guided there is no fee. When you request a mentor, schedule a check-in or look at your check-ins, the app shows you the total, with the fee on its own line.
- **Credit is spent at the check-in.** When your mentor submits a check-in, or you confirm one that took place outside the app, that tier's price plus any service fee is taken from your balance.
- **Say thank you.** You can also send your mentor a one-off payment with a short note, for example to thank them for an extra session. It is separate from the tiers, comes out of your balance the same way, and needs enough credit when you send it.

How often you meet is agreed with the mentor.

mentee_working.title: Mentors: working with a mentor
mentee_working.text:
## Working with a mentor

Once connected, you have a direct chat with your mentor for the back and forth between check-ins.

You choose which of your quests your mentor can open, one quest at a time, under My mentors. Each quest is Not shared, View (your mentor sees the whole quest dashboard but cannot change it) or Edit (your mentor can also edit it). Your mentor sees only the quests you share, and you can change or stop sharing at any time. With a quest shared, the conversation stays grounded in your actual plan and progress.

A mentor supports and advises you. You still own your quest and your decisions.

If you choose it for a metric (How this is recorded, My mentor drafts or Either), a mentor of a quest you shared can propose a value for it. Their proposal appears on that metric for you to confirm or correct, and nothing is written into your collections until you do. Mentors see these requests on their dashboard.

### Bringing in your AI (optional)

You can optionally bring your own AI into a mentor chat using the sparkle button in the header. This is off by default and talking to your mentor never requires AI. It only affects your side: turning your AI on adds your own AI to the chat so you can ask it things in context, and turning it off removes it again. Your mentor controls their side the same way, and neither side can bring in the other's AI. When you have more than one AI rep, you pick which one to bring in.

mentor_become.title: Mentors: becoming a mentor
mentor_become.text:
## Becoming a mentor

If you want to guide others, you can apply to become a mentor. The application asks about your experience and credentials, which can include documents, links, and testimonials, and goes through an evaluation. Mentors are placed at a level that reflects their experience, and can be re-evaluated as they grow.

### Earnings and payouts

You set your own check-in tiers: named packages, each with one fixed price per check-in, so mentees choose a tier and never an amount. When you complete a check-in, or your mentee confirms one that took place outside the app, the tier's price for that session is added to your earnings as pending credit. Any service fee your mentee pays is added on top of your price and never reduces it. A one-off payment from a mentee, sent with a note, is added the same way. Pending credit becomes available after a short waiting period, which is a Quest policy setting shown in the app. The waiting period exists so that a refund or dispute can cancel the earnings before they are paid out. If your mentee's payment has not come through yet, the check-in still completes and your earnings stay on hold until their payment settles. A platform fee, if Quest applies one, is taken when the earnings are recorded and never changes earnings already recorded.

Your balance shows what is pending, what is available, and your history of earnings and withdrawals in one place. Available earnings can pay for your own mentorship or be withdrawn to your bank. To withdraw, set up payouts once through the secure Stripe onboarding in the app. Withdrawals need a minimum amount, which is a Quest policy setting shown in the app, and earnings below it keep building until they reach it. Quest also sends available earnings automatically every few hours once payout set-up is complete and the minimum is met.

Payout set-up is not available in every country. If it is not available where you live, your earnings stay in your account, you can spend them on your own mentorship, and the app tells you that withdrawal is not available for your country.

account_profile.title: Account settings: profile, appearance and time
account_profile.text:
Manage your profile, privacy, notifications, and data from **Settings** in the app. This page is an overview of what is there.

## Profile

Set your display name, edit your bio, and upload a profile photo. This is separate from your community [character](/guide/communities#your-character), which is the identity (name, bio, and 3D avatar) you use in towns and planets.

## Appearance and time

- **Theme:** switch between light and dark mode.
- **Time zone:** set your time zone, or let Quest detect it. Your Today, Schedule, and period reviews use it to decide what counts as today, this week, and so on.

account_language.title: Account settings: language
account_language.text:
## Language

Quest's interface is available in English and Español. Change it in **Settings > Language**: tap it, then pick your language from the list. The app switches right away, no restart needed.

Your choice is saved with your account, so it carries over to every device you sign into.

Switching languages changes the interface: navigation, buttons, labels, error messages, onboarding, and settings. It also translates Quest's world content: planet, town, and category names and descriptions, and the built-in character species. It does not change what you have written. Your quest titles, notes, and descriptions always display in the language you wrote them in. Quest AI already matches your language on its own: write to it in Español and it answers in Español, no setting required.

If a translation is not ready yet for a piece of text, Quest shows it in English rather than leaving a blank.

More languages are planned.

account_notifications.title: Account settings: notifications
account_notifications.text:
## Notifications

The bell in the header opens your **Notifications** page: everything Quest has told you, in one list.

- **Filter at the top:** All, Quests (asks, AI task results, goal and habit reminders, quest invitations), Social (mentor messages, chat replies and mentions, community activity) and System (account, bookings, data). Each filter shows how many unread items it holds.
- **Each row says what a tap does**, for example "Open ask", "Open AI task", "Open habit" or "Open team chat". A notification with nowhere to go says "Tap to mark read" instead.
- **Remove a notification** with the X on its row. You get five seconds to Undo before it is gone for good. **Clear** removes read notifications, or all of them, after you confirm. Unread chats are not stored notifications, so they stay in the list until you open the chat.
- **Mark all read** clears every unread badge at once. Older notifications load with **Show older notifications**.
- The gear in the page header opens the notification settings below.

Control how Quest reaches you:

- Turn push and email notifications on or off. **Push** covers everything that arrives on a device, including the habit and goal reminders Quest schedules for your set times, so turning it off silences those as well.
- Choose which categories you want, including habits, quests, mentors, community, chat, and account updates.
- Toggle **habit and goal reminders** for the actions you scheduled, and choose whether alarm-style habits may ring as full alarms.
- Manage your **notification devices**: see every phone and browser registered to your account, pick which one is primary, register the device you are on, and remove any you no longer use.

calendar_google.title: Calendar Sync: connect Google Calendar
calendar_google.text:
# Calendar Sync

Calendar Sync connects your real calendar to Quest, in both directions. Your existing events help Quest and its AI understand when you are actually free, and your Quest schedule can show up on your calendar alongside everything else in your life.

You manage it from **Settings > Calendar Sync**. There are two kinds of calendar connection, and you can use either or both. The same screen also has an **Email** section for connecting your Google email read-only; that is a separate feature covered in [Quest AI: Email](/guide/quest-ai#email), not part of calendar sync. One link between them: when Quest AI proposes a goal from an email (an interview time, a deadline) and you approve it, it becomes an ordinary goal and Calendar Sync puts it on your calendar like any other goal; nothing reaches your calendar before you approve.

## Connect a device calendar

## Connect Google Calendar

In the **Google Calendar** section, tap **Connect Google Calendar** and sign in with your Google account in the browser. This is a direct connection between Quest's servers and Google, so once it is set up it keeps syncing on its own even when the app is closed.

**If you are asked to sign in to Quest on the way back from Google**, nothing has gone wrong and nothing has to be approved at Google again. Sign in and Quest takes you straight back to Calendar Sync and finishes the connection. The sign-in screen says so while a connection is waiting.

**If the connection does not finish straight away**, the Calendar Sync screen shows a **Finish connecting Google Calendar** card with how long is left, and one tap finishes it. The approval you gave Google is held for 15 minutes, so this is almost always quicker than connecting again. Past 15 minutes, or if the card says to connect again, tap **Connect Google Calendar** and approve once more.

**If the connection fails**, a red banner on the Calendar Sync screen says why, and nothing was connected. The reasons you can see:

- **Google did not allow the connection.** The permission was declined, or your Google account is not approved for this connection yet. Try again and tick every permission box. If it keeps happening, tell us which Google account you used.
- **The sign-in took too long, or the link was already used.** Tap **Connect Google Calendar** once and finish in a single pass, without going back or tapping twice.
- **Google sent you back before it finished, or approved it but Quest could not finish setting it up.** Try again.

After connecting, your Google calendars appear as a list. Turn on the ones you want in Quest; each becomes its own connection with its own settings. A calendar that is read-only in your Google account (for example, one someone shared with you) can still bring its events into Quest, but Quest cannot write your schedule to it. A fresh Google connection starts exactly like a fresh device one, so read "What a fresh connection does, and does not, do yet" above before wondering why nothing moved.

calendar_where.title: Calendar Sync: where your events show up
calendar_where.text:
## Where your events show up

Events from every calendar with "Show events on Quest and use for AI scheduling" on appear on **Today** and on **Schedule**, in their real time slots, next to your goals and habits. If a calendar you turned on shows nothing, that setting is where to look first.

account_delete.title: Delete your account
account_delete.text:
## How to Delete Your Account

### Step 1: Open Settings

1. Open the Quest app on your device
2. Tap the **Settings** icon (gear icon) in the navigation bar

### Step 2: Find Delete Account Option

1. Scroll down to the **Account** section
2. Tap **Delete Account** (shown in red text)

### Step 3: Review What Will Be Deleted

1. A confirmation screen will appear showing:
   - A summary of all data that will be deleted
   - The number of quests, collections, entries, and other records
2. Optionally select a reason for leaving (helps us improve Quest)
3. Tap **Continue to Delete** to proceed

### Step 4: Confirm Deletion

1. Type `DELETE MY ACCOUNT` exactly as shown to confirm
2. Tap the **Delete My Account** button
3. Wait for the deletion to complete

- All your data will be permanently removed within 30 days

exporting.title: Your data and the API: exporting
exporting.text:
## Exporting

You do not need the API to get your data out. Any [Data Collection](/data-collections/#exporting-your-data) exports to **CSV, JSON, TXT, or PDF** from the app. For programmatic access to the rest, use the API below.

quest_ai_intro.title: Quest AI: what you can ask
quest_ai_intro.text:
# Quest AI

Quest AI is the assistant built into the app. It is a single chat that knows your quests, your plans, and your progress, so you can ask for help in plain language instead of clicking through screens.

You reach it from **Quest AI** in the navigation. It opens as a general chat by default, and you can point it at a specific quest when you want it focused there.

## What you can ask

Quest AI answers questions and takes actions on your quests. For example:

- "Explain what this strategy is based on."
- "Add a habit to meditate 10 minutes every weekday morning."
- "My schedule changed. Rework this plan around weekends only."
- "Summarize where I am on my fitness quest."
- "Suggest a goal for next week based on how this week went."

Replies are formatted for easy reading, and you will see a working indicator while it thinks. Requests that change a quest, like adding a goal, happen right there in the chat.

quest_ai_web.title: Quest AI: current information from the web
quest_ai_web.text:
## Current information from the web

When a question depends on something that changes in the world, like a release date, a price, a race schedule, or the latest version of a tool, Quest AI looks it up on the web before answering. You will see "Searching the web…" while it does, and "Reading a web page…" when it needs the full text of one page. You can also paste a link to a public page and ask about it.

Answers that use the web cite their sources as links right in the reply, so you can open the page and check it yourself. In [Voice Mode](/guide/voice-mode), the links stay in the transcript and only the words are spoken.

Quest AI does not search the web for your own quests, goals, or notes, or for small talk. Those answers come from your Quest data. If web search is unavailable, Quest AI answers from what it already knows and tells you the information may be out of date.

quest_ai_now_later.title: Quest AI: doing work now, or later
quest_ai_now_later.text:
## Doing work now, or later

Some requests are quick and run in the moment. Others are open-ended and take time. Quest AI can handle both.

- **In the moment:** "add a goal to this quest" runs inline and you see the result immediately.
- **Handed off:** when you ask for something to be done later, overnight, or on a schedule ("research three standing desks under $400 and report back", "draft my weekly update tomorrow morning"), Quest AI recognizes the hand-off and turns it into a task for your assistant. You can watch its progress and read the result when it is done.

Handing work off is part of the [Productivity workflow](/guide/productivity), which also covers the Assistant setting that turns delegation on, scheduling tasks, and reviewing what your assistant did.

ai_tasks_intro.title: AI Tasks: what they are
ai_tasks_intro.text:
# AI Tasks

AI Tasks are pieces of work you hand to your AI to do in the background. You delegate a task, the AI works on it, and it reports back when it is done. You do not have to wait around. You can keep using Quest while it works, and check on the result later.

There are four ways a task gets created:

- **From your daily reflection.** The "Tasks for your assistant" field turns each line you write into a queued task.
- **From the Add button.** On the AI Tasks page, tap Add and write what you want done.
- **From Quest AI chat.** When you ask for something open-ended or scheduled, like "research three standing desks under $400 and report back tomorrow", Quest AI turns it into a task instead of answering inline. The task gets its title, quest, team and environment filled in the same way the **Delegate to AI** form fills them, so it lands on the right quest even when you asked from a general chat.

When a chat request needs your team's server or runner environment (checking server logs, running something on that machine, work only that environment can do), Quest AI routes the task to that environment automatically, even from a general chat with no quest selected. And when one message bundles clearly separate pieces of work (say, a server check and some web research), Quest AI splits it into one task per piece, each with its own live card in the chat, so you can follow, open, or cancel each part on its own.

When several of your quests are in the chat and Quest AI cannot tell which one a task belongs to, it asks once, listing up to three of them and offering "no quest". Answer with the quest's name or number, or say "no quest" (or ask for an independent or standalone task up front) and the task is created without one. You can also name any quest of your own, even one that is not part of this chat. Quest AI never asks the same question twice in a row: if your answer still does not match a quest, it creates the task without a quest, says which name it could not find, and you can attach it later by giving the exact quest name.
- **From team chat.** Tap **Make this a task** on any AI team member's message to queue that message as a real task. A confirmation reads "Queued as an AI task." A "View task" link appears once it is queued.

For how delegation fits the wider rhythm of planning and reviewing, see the [Productivity workflow](/guide/productivity).

ai_tasks_types.title: AI Tasks: the Type filter
ai_tasks_types.text: - **Type:** what kind of work the task is. **Quest operation** (a change to your Quest data, such as adding a goal from chat), **Web search**, **Docs lookup**, **External environment** (a deep run on one of your team's connected runners), or **Other** for older tasks recorded before types existed. You do not need an external environment to have tasks: a Quest operation or a web search is a task like any other, listed and filtered here with the rest.

ai_tasks_followup.title: AI Tasks: follow-up work
ai_tasks_followup.text: **Follow-up work stays on the plan.** A task started from another task belongs to the same quest and the same goal as the task it came from. When an AI rep or Autopilot starts follow-up work, it says which goal that work serves: an existing goal, or a new sub-goal it creates under the goal it was working on, with an owner, a deadline and the outcome it moves. If a goal already stands for the work, it uses that goal instead of adding a duplicate. When the new goal belongs to a teammate, the task runs in that teammate's AI lane.

workflows_intro.title: Workflows: what they are and how to start one
workflows_intro.text:
# Workflows

A workflow shows who does what, and when, as a diagram: steps joined by arrows. Each step is run either by a person on your team or by one of your AI representatives, and each one says what needs to happen and by when. Quest watches whether it actually happened, so a missed step shows up as a risk instead of going unnoticed.

Workflows belong to a **team** or an **organization**, not to a single quest. One workflow can touch several quests, and a step can be tagged with the quest it belongs to.

## Where to find Workflows

- Open the menu (the hamburger icon), expand **AI Productivity**, then tap **Workflows**. The same entry is on your Profile page under AI Productivity.
- On a team's page, tap the **Workflows** row. It opens the same screen with that team already selected.

Like the rest of AI Productivity, Workflows is part of the paid plans.

Tap **New workflow** in the switcher, or the button in an empty list. Give it a name, choose the team or organization it is for, and start in one of four ways:

- **Describe it and let AI draft it**: say what the workflow is for and who is involved. The AI drafts it, you see the draft as a diagram marked "Draft, not live yet", and you can ask for changes ("make the reply due sooner"). Each request is saved in a feedback history with a one-line summary of what changed, and you can look back at an earlier version. Nothing runs until you choose **Create workflow**.

ai_reps_intro.title: AI representatives
ai_reps_intro.text:
# AI representatives

An AI representative (an "AI rep") is your own AI counterpart in Quest. It is the version of [Quest AI](/guide/quest-ai) that acts as you: it carries your context, works in your voice, and can run work on your behalf. Everyone has one by default, and you can add more for different areas of your work.

If you are on a [team](/guide/teams), your default rep is also how teammates interact with "you" in AI: when someone brings your rep into a chat or hands it a task, it answers grounded in your context and preferences.

## Your default rep

You always have exactly one **default rep**. If you have never set one up, Quest creates it for you automatically the first time it is needed, named from your profile. The default is the rep that:

- represents you to others on your team, and
- conducts a chat or runs a task when no specific rep is chosen.

You can change which rep is your default at any time (see below).

- **Create another rep** for a specific area, for example a "research" rep and a "writing" rep, each with its own focus.

- **Edit how a rep acts.** Give it a name, a short description of its area, and a persona (instructions for how it should respond as you). A persona can be at most 8,000 characters: keep it to who the rep is, how it speaks and its few standing rules.

science_intro.title: Science
science_intro.text:
# Science

Science is where you look at the evidence on any question: published research papers and first-hand accounts of human experience, from every field. [Quest AI](/guide/quest-ai) is for talking through your own quests and life. Science is for finding out what is actually known.

Open it from the navigation menu. It has three modes, shown as tabs at the top.

Direct finds matching papers and experiences instantly.
